sentences.zh: 蠻

translations.literal: The Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Man.

sentences.zh: 蠻，種類繁多，言語不一，咸依山谷，布荊、湘、雍、郢、司等五州界。

translations.literal: The Man: their kinds are extremely numerous and their languages not uniform; all rely on valleys and ravines, and are spread across the borders of the five provinces Jing, Xiang, Yong, Ying, and Si.
translations.idiomatic: The Man peoples were of countless branches and spoke many tongues; they all dwelt in mountain valleys, scattered along the frontiers of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Ying, and Si provinces.

sentences.zh: 宋世封西陽蠻梅蟲生為高山侯，田治生為威山侯，梅加羊為扞山侯。

translations.literal: In the Song era, the Xiyang Man Mei Chong sheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoshan, Tian Zhi sheng as Marquis of Weishan, and Mei Jiayang as Marquis of Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song dynasty, the court enfeoffed the Xiyang Man chieftains Mei Chong sheng as Marquis of Gaoshan, Tian Zhi sheng as Marquis of Weishan, and Mei Jiayang as Marquis of Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，有司奏蠻封應在解例，參議以：「戎夷疏爵，理章列代；

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, the relevant offices memorialized that Man enfeoffments should fall under the statute for dismissal; deliberators held: 'For the Rong and Yi, distant enfeoffments are prescribed in the institutions of successive dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: After the founding emperor took the throne, officials reported that Man titles should be abolished under the usual rules for dismissing fiefs; deliberators argued that distant enfeoffments for Rong and Yi peoples were established in the institutions of past dynasties,

sentences.zh: 酋豪世襲，事炳前葉。

translations.literal: chieftains inherit by generations, a matter clear in earlier records.
translations.idiomatic: their chieftains held hereditary rank, as records of earlier ages make plain.

sentences.zh: 今宸曆改物，舊冊枃降，而梅生等保落奉政，事須繩總，恩命升贊，有異常品。

translations.literal: Now the celestial succession has changed things and old registers are reduced, yet Mei Sheng and the rest preserve their settlements and observe government; the matter must be brought under regulation, yet grace raised them in support—an exceptional case.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the dynasty had changed and old registers were being scaled back, Mei Sheng and others still held their domains and answered to the government—a case that demanded oversight—yet imperial favor had raised them to titles beyond ordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 謂宜存名以訓殊俗。」

translations.literal: They held that titles ought to be kept to instruct alien customs.'
translations.idiomatic: They argued that the titles should be retained to instruct these foreign peoples.'

sentences.zh: 詔：「特留。」

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Retain them especially.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: 'Let them be retained.'

sentences.zh: 以治生為輔國將軍、虎賁中郎，轉建寧郡太守，將軍、侯如故。

translations.literal: Tian Zhi sheng was made General Assistant to the State and Tiger-Fang Central Commander, then transferred to Administrator of Jianning Commandery, his generalship and marquisate remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhi sheng was appointed General Assistant to the State and Tiger-Fang Central Commander, later transferred to Administrator of Jianning Commandery while keeping his general's title and marquisate unchanged.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，虜侵豫、司，蠻中傳虜已近，又聞官盡發民丁，南襄城蠻秦遠以郡縣無備，寇潼陽，縣令焦文度戰死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, the Wei barbarians invaded Yu and Si; among the Man it was rumored that the barbarians were near, and it was also heard that the authorities were conscripting all civilian males. The Nanxiangcheng Man Qin Yuan, because the commandery and counties were unprepared, raided Tongyang; the magistrate Jiao Wendu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 2, Northern Wei forces invaded Yu and Si provinces; among the Man peoples word spread that the enemy was close, and that the government was drafting every able-bodied man. The Nanxiangcheng Man chieftain Qin Yuan, finding the counties undefended, attacked Tongyang, and Magistrate Jiao Wendu was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 司州蠻引虜攻平昌戍，戍主苟元賓擊破之。

translations.literal: The Man of Si Province led the barbarians to attack the Pingchang garrison; the garrison commander Gou Yuanbin defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Man bands in Si Province brought Wei troops against the Pingchang garrison, but Garrison Commander Gou Yuanbin routed them.

sentences.zh: 秦遠又出破臨沮百方砦，殺略百餘人。

translations.literal: Qin Yuan again came forth, defeated the Baifang stockade of Linju, and killed and plundered more than a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Yuan struck again, overrunning the Baifang stockade near Linju and killing or carrying off more than a hundred people.

sentences.zh: 北上黃蠻文勉德寇汶陽，太守戴元孫孤城力弱，慮不自保，棄戍歸江陵。

translations.literal: The Beishanghuang Man Wen Miande raided Wenyang; Administrator Dai Yuansun, with an isolated city and weak forces, feared he could not hold out, abandoned the garrison, and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Beishanghuang Man Wen Miande attacked Wenyang; Administrator Dai Yuansun, holding a lone outpost with too few men to defend it, abandoned the post and withdrew to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史豫章王遣中兵參軍劉伾緒領千人討勉德，至當陽，勉德請降，收其部落，使戍汶陽所治城子，令保持商旅，付其清通，遠遂逃竄。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Yuzhang, sent Central Army Major Liu Pixu at the head of a thousand men to attack Miande; when they reached Dangyang, Miande requested surrender. His tribes were taken in hand, stationed to guard the walled town administered by Wenyang, ordered to keep the roads safe for merchants and travelers, and charged with keeping communications clear; Yuan then fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou Inspector the Prince of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Liu Pixu with a thousand troops against Miande. At Dangyang, Miande surrendered; his followers were enrolled to garrison the walled town under Wenyang's jurisdiction, charged with safeguarding merchants on the roads and keeping the routes open, while Qin Yuan fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 汶陽本臨沮西界，二百里中，水陸迂狹，魚貫而行，有數處不通騎，而水白田甚肥腴。

translations.literal: Wenyang was originally the western border of Linju; within two hundred li, by water and land the routes were winding and narrow, passable only in single file, and in several places impassable to mounted riders, yet the flooded fields were very fertile.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyang had originally marked the western edge of Linju. For two hundred li the land and water routes wound through narrow defiles where men had to pass single file; in several stretches cavalry could not go at all, yet the irrigated fields were richly fertile.

sentences.zh: 桓溫時，割以為郡。

translations.literal: In Huan Wen's time it was carved out as a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Wen it was carved out as a separate commandery.

sentences.zh: 西北接梁州新城，東北接南襄城，南接巴、巫二邊，竝山蠻凶盛，據險為寇賊。

translations.literal: To the northwest it adjoined Xincheng in Liang Province; to the northeast it adjoined Nanxiangcheng; to the south it adjoined the Ba and Wu frontiers. The mountain Man on both sides were fierce and strong, holding the passes to act as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Liangzhou's Xincheng on the northwest and Nanxiangcheng on the northeast, and met the Ba and Wu marches on the south. Mountain Man on every side were powerful and used the terrain to raid as bandits.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始以來，巴建蠻向宗頭反，刺史沈攸之斷其鹽米，連討不剋。

translations.literal: From the Taishi era of Song onward, the Bajian Man Xiang Zongtou rebelled; Inspector Shen Youzhi cut off their salt and grain, yet successive campaigns could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song Taishi reign onward the Bajian Man chieftain Xiang Zongtou rebelled; Inspector Shen Youzhi cut off his salt and grain supplies, but repeated campaigns failed to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 晉

translations.literal: Jin
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin

translations.literal: Corrupt: tian.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔太〕興三年，建平夷王向弘、向瓂等詣臺求拜除，尚書郎張亮議：「夷貊不可假以軍號。」

translations.literal: [Supplied: Tai]xing year 3, the Pingjian Yi king Xiang Hong, Xiang Qiong, and others came to the court requesting appointment and dismissal [of office]; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Zhang Liang deliberated: 'Yi and Mo must not be lent military titles.'
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jin Taixing, the Pingjian Yi king Xiang Hong and Xiang Qiong and others came to court seeking formal appointments; Zhang Liang of the Secretariat argued that barbarian peoples must not be granted military titles.

sentences.zh: 元帝詔特以弘為折衝將軍、當平鄉侯，竝親晉王，賜以朝服。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan nonetheless specially made Hong General Who Breaks the Charge and Marquis of Dangping Township, ranking him with the Prince of Jin, and bestowed court robes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan nonetheless appointed Hong General Who Breaks the Charge and Marquis of Dangping Township, ranking him alongside the Prince of Jin, and granted him court dress.

sentences.zh: 宗頭其後也。

translations.literal: Zongtou was his descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zongtou was descended from him.

sentences.zh: 太祖置巴州以威靜之。

translations.literal: The Taizu established Ba Province to awe and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor established Ba Province to overawe and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 其武陵酉溪蠻田思飄寇抄，內史王文和討之，引軍深入，蠻自後斷其糧。

translations.literal: The Wuling Youxi Man Tian Sipiao raided and plundered; Internal Historian Wang Wenhe attacked them, led his army deep in, and the Man cut off his supplies from behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuling Youxi Man Tian Sipiao raided the countryside; Internal Historian Wang Wenhe marched against him, advancing deep into Man territory, where the tribes cut his supply lines from the rear.

sentences.zh: 豫章王遣中兵參軍莊明五百人將湘州鎮兵合千人救之，思飄與文和拒戰，中弩矢死，蠻眾以城降。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Zhuang Ming with five hundred men, leading Xiangzhou garrison troops for a combined force of a thousand to rescue them; Sipiao fought Wenhe in resistance, was struck by a crossbow bolt and died, and the Man masses surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Zhuang Ming with five hundred men, together with Xiangzhou garrison troops, a thousand in all, to relieve the column. Sipiao met Wenhe in battle, took a crossbow bolt and died, and his followers surrendered the fortress.

sentences.zh: 永明初，向宗頭與黔陽蠻田豆渠等五千人為寇，巴東太守王圖南遣府司馬劉僧壽等斬山開道，攻其砦，宗頭夜燒砦退走。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming, Xiang Zongtou together with the Qianyang Man Tian Douqu and others, five thousand men, made raids; Administrator of Badong Wang Tunan sent his headquarters Major Liu Shoushou and others to cut through the mountains and open roads, attacked their stockade, and Zongtou burned the stockade by night and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongming era, Xiang Zongtou and the Qianyang Man Tian Douqu led five thousand raiders. Badong Administrator Wang Tunan sent Headquarters Major Liu Shoushou and others to hew paths through the mountains and assault their stockade; Zongtou burned the camp by night and fled.

sentences.zh: 三年，湘川蠻陳雙、李答寇掠郡縣，刺史呂安國討之不克。

translations.literal: In year 3, the Xiangchuan Man Chen Shuang and Li Da raided and plundered commanderies and counties; Inspector Lu Anguo attacked them but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 the Xiangchuan Man Chen Shuang and Li Da plundered the commanderies and counties; Inspector Lu Anguo campaigned against them without success.

sentences.zh: 四年，刺史柳世隆督眾征討，乃平。

translations.literal: In year 4, Inspector Liu Shilong supervised the masses in campaign and punishment, and then they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Inspector Liu Shilong led a combined force against them and finally pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 五年，雍、司州蠻與虜通，助荒人桓天生為亂。

translations.literal: In year 5, the Man of Yong and Si provinces communicated with the barbarians and aided the wilderness people Huan Tiansheng in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the Man of Yong and Si provinces colluded with the Wei enemy and aided the renegade Huan Tiansheng in revolt.

sentences.zh: 六年，除督護北遂安左郡太守田駟路為試守北遂安左郡太守，前寧朔將軍田驢王〔為試守宜人左郡太守，田何代〕為試守新平左郡太守，皆郢州蠻也。

translations.literal: In year 6, Tian Silu, Supervisor-Protector and Administrator of North Sui'an Left Commandery, was appointed trial Administrator of North Sui'an Left Commandery; the former General Ning Shuo Tian Lüwang [was appointed trial Administrator of Yiren Left Commandery, Tian Hedai] was appointed trial Administrator of Xinping Left Commandery—all were Man of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Tian Silu, who had served as Supervisor-Protector and Administrator of North Sui'an Left Commandery, was confirmed as acting Administrator of that district; former General Ning Shuo Tian Lüwang was made acting Administrator of Yiren Left Commandery and Tian Hedai acting Administrator of Xinping Left Commandery—all of them Man chieftains from Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 九年，安隆內史王僧旭發民丁，遣寬城戍主萬民和助八百丁村蠻伐千二百丁村蠻，為蠻所敗，民和被傷，失馬及器仗，有司奏免官。

translations.literal: In year 9, Anlong Internal Historian Wang Xuxu conscripted civilian males and sent Kuancheng Garrison Commander Wan Minhe to aid the eight-hundred-ding village Man in attacking the twelve-hundred-ding village Man; they were defeated by the Man, Minhe was wounded, and horses and weapons were lost; the relevant offices memorialized for his dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Anlong Internal Historian Wang Xuxu drafted militia and sent Kuancheng Garrison Commander Wan Minhe to help an eight-hundred-household Man village fight a twelve-hundred-household Man village. The Man routed them; Minhe was wounded and lost horses and arms, and officials memorialized for his removal.

sentences.zh: 西陽蠻田益宗，沈攸之時，以功勞得將領，遂為臨川王防閤，叛投虜，虜以為東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The Xiyang Man Tian Yizong, in Shen Youzhi's time, through merit and toil obtained a general's post, then became Defender of the Prince of Linchuan, defected and went over to the barbarians, and the barbarians made him Inspector of Eastern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiyang Man Tian Yizong had won a commander's post through service under Shen Youzhi and became Defender of the Prince of Linchuan, then defected to the Wei and was appointed their Inspector of Eastern Yu.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，虜遣益宗攻司州龍城戍，為戍主朱僧起所破。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, the barbarians sent Yizong to attack the Longcheng garrison of Si Province; he was defeated by Garrison Commander Zhu Senqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 3 the Wei sent Yizong against the Longcheng garrison in Si Province, but Garrison Commander Zhu Senqi defeated him.

sentences.zh: 蠻俗衣布徒跣，或椎髻，或翦髮。

translations.literal: Man custom: they wear cloth and go barefoot, or wear topknots, or cut their hair short.
translations.idiomatic: Man custom was to wear cloth and go barefoot; some wore topknots, others cropped their hair.

sentences.zh: 兵器以金銀為飾，虎皮衣楯，便弩射，皆暴悍好寇賊焉。

translations.literal: Their weapons are ornamented with gold and silver; they wear tiger-skin coats and carry shields, are skilled at crossbow shooting, and all are fierce and violent, fond of banditry.
translations.idiomatic: They ornamented their weapons with gold and silver, wore tiger hides and carried shields, excelled with the crossbow, and were by nature fierce and prone to raiding.

sentences.zh: 東夷

translations.literal: Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 高麗國

translations.literal: The state of Gaoli.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: =東夷高麗國，西與魏虜接界。

translations.literal: The Eastern Yi state of Gaoli borders the Wei barbarians on the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi state of Goguryeo shared its western border with Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 宋末，高麗王樂浪公高璉為使持節、散騎常侍、都督營平二州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, the King of Gaoli, Duke of Lelang Gao Lian, held the posts of Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the two provinces Ying and Ping, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Tally equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song, Goguryeo's King Gao Lian, Duke of Lelang, held Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Ying and Ping provinces, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Tally equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太祖建元元年，進號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan year 1 of the Taizu, his title was advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding emperor's first Jianyuan year his title was raised to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使貢獻，乘舶汎海，使驛常通，亦使魏虜，然彊盛不受制。

translations.literal: In year 3 he sent envoys with tribute, crossing the sea by ship; courier stations were kept in constant communication, and envoys also went to the Wei barbarians, yet being powerful and flourishing they were not controlled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he sent tribute missions by sea; courier routes stayed open, and embassies went to Northern Wei as well, yet Goguryeo was strong enough to remain beyond anyone's control.

sentences.zh: 虜置諸國使邸，齊使第一，高麗次之。

translations.literal: The barbarians established lodges for the envoys of the various states: Qi envoys ranked first, Gaoli next.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei set up hostels for foreign envoys, ranking Qi first and Goguryeo second.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，平南參軍顏幼明、冗從僕射劉思斅使虜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming, Pacification of the South Major Yan Youming and Supernumerary Attendant of the Retinue Liu Sixie were envoys to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 7 Yan Youming, Pacification of the South Major, and Liu Sixie, Supernumerary Attendant of the Retinue, were sent as envoys to the Wei court.

sentences.zh: 虜元會，與高麗使相次。

translations.literal: At the barbarians' New Year assembly, they followed the Gaoli envoys in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wei New Year audience they were placed immediately after the Goguryeo envoys.

sentences.zh: 幼明謂偽主客郎裴叔令曰：「我等銜命上華，來造卿國。

translations.literal: Youming said to the false Master of Guests Gentleman Pei Shuling: 'We bear orders from the Upper Flowering [dynasty] and have come to visit your state.
translations.idiomatic: Youming told the Wei Master of Guests Pei Shuling, 'We bear orders from the southern court and have come to your realm.

sentences.zh: 所為抗敵，在乎一魏。

translations.literal: Our purpose in standing as rivals lies in Wei alone.
translations.idiomatic: Our only peer in rivalry is Wei.

sentences.zh: 自餘外夷，理不得望我鑣塵。

translations.literal: All other outer barbarians, by right, ought not to look upon our chariot dust.
translations.idiomatic: Every other foreign people ought not even to glimpse our chariot dust.

sentences.zh: 況東夷小貊，臣屬朝廷，今日乃敢與我躡踵。」

translations.literal: How much more the small Mo of the Eastern Yi, subjects of the court—today they dare tread on our heels!'
translations.idiomatic: As for that petty Mo people of the Eastern Yi, subjects of our court—how dare they today step on our heels!'

sentences.zh: 思斅謂偽南部尚書李思沖曰：「我聖朝處魏使，未嘗與小國列，卿亦應知。」

translations.literal: Sixie said to the false Southern Department Minister Li Sichong: 'Our sage dynasty places Wei envoys and has never ranked them with small states—you ought to know this as well.'
translations.idiomatic: Sixie told the Wei Southern Department Minister Li Sichong, 'Our sacred court has never seated Wei envoys alongside petty states—you know that as well as I.

sentences.zh: 思沖曰：「實如此。

translations.literal: Sichong said: 'It is truly so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sichong replied, 'That is indeed so.

sentences.zh: 但主副不得升殿耳。

translations.literal: Only the chief and deputy may not ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Only the chief envoy and his deputy may not ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 此閒坐起甚高，足以相報。」

translations.literal: The seats here for sitting and rising are very high—enough to answer you in kind.'
translations.idiomatic: The seats provided here are set quite high—high enough to answer you in kind.'

sentences.zh: 思斅曰：「李道固昔使，正以衣冠致隔耳。

translations.literal: Sixie said: 'When Li Daogu was envoy in the past, it was precisely robes and caps that caused the separation.
translations.idiomatic: Sixie said, 'When Li Daogu came as envoy, the separation was only a matter of court dress.

sentences.zh: 魏國必纓冕而至，豈容見黜。」

translations.literal: The state of Wei will surely come in caps and coronets—how could it be allowed to be demoted?'
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei come they will surely wear full regalia—how could they be demoted?'

sentences.zh: 幼明又謂虜主曰：「二國相亞，唯齊與魏。

translations.literal: Youming again said to the barbarian ruler: 'Of two states that stand as peers, only Qi and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Youming also told the Wei ruler, 'Only two states stand as equals—Qi and Wei.

sentences.zh: 邊境小狄，敢躡臣蹤。」

translations.literal: A petty Di on the border dares tread on a minister's tracks.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet some petty Di on the frontier dares step on a minister's heels!'

sentences.zh: 高麗俗服窮袴，冠折風一梁，謂之幘。

translations.literal: Gaoli custom: dress of narrow trousers, a cap with one crossbeam of folded wind, called a ze.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo custom favored narrow trousers and a cap with a single crosswise rib, called a ze.

sentences.zh: 知讀五經。

translations.literal: They know how to read the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: They could read the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 使人在京師，中書郎王融戯之曰：「服之不衷，身之災也。

translations.literal: When an envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong jested with him, saying: 'Dress not at the center is a bodily calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When a Goguryeo envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong teased him, quoting, 'Dress that is not centered brings bodily disaster.

sentences.zh: 頭上定是何物？」

translations.literal: What exactly is that on your head?'
translations.idiomatic: What in the world is that on your head?'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「此即古弁之遺像也。」

translations.literal: He answered: 'This is the surviving image of the ancient bian cap.'
translations.idiomatic: The envoy replied, 'This is the ancient ceremonial cap preserved from antiquity.'

sentences.zh: 高璉年百餘歲卒。

translations.literal: Gao Lian died at more than a hundred years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lian died at over a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以高麗王樂浪公高雲為使持節、散騎常侍、都督營平二州諸軍事、征東大將軍、高麗王、樂浪公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang, Gao Yun, King of Gaoli and Duke of Lelang, was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the two provinces Ying and Ping, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Gaoli, and Duke of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 Gao Yun was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Ying and Ping, Grand General Who Conquers the East, King of Goguryeo, and Duke of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu,
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 3,

sentences.zh: 〈原闕〉

translations.literal: 〈Original text missing.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Original text missing.〉

sentences.zh: 報功勞勤，實存名烈。

translations.literal: To repay merit and toil with diligence truly preserves a name of glory.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarding merit and loyal toil truly preserves a name for posterity.

sentences.zh: 假行寧朔將軍臣姐瑾等四人，振竭忠効，攘除國難，志勇果毅，等威名將，可謂扞城，固蕃社稷，論功料勤，宜在甄顯。

translations.literal: The acting General Ning Shuo, subject Jie Jin, and four others have exhausted their loyalty and efficacy, swept away national peril, and in will, courage, and resoluteness equal famous generals; they may be called bulwarks of the city, securing the altars of state and grain; in weighing merit and measuring toil, they ought to be selected for prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Acting General Ning Shuo Jie Jin and three others have given their utmost loyalty, cleared away national danger, and in courage and resolve rival famed commanders—they are bulwarks of the realm and pillars of the altars of state; by their merits they deserve special recognition.

sentences.zh: 今依例輒假行職。

translations.literal: Now, according to precedent, acting posts are forthwith granted.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore grant them acting appointments according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 伏願恩愍，聽除所假。

translations.literal: I bow and hope for gracious compassion, that you hear and confirm what has been granted in acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg your gracious approval to confirm these acting appointments.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、面中王姐瑾，歷贊時務，武功竝列，今假行冠軍將軍、都將軍、都漢王。

translations.literal: General Ning Shuo, King of Mianzhong Jie Jin, having assisted in affairs through the ages with martial achievements standing side by side, is now granted acting rank as General Who Wins the Championship, Commander-in-Chief of the Army, and King of Duhan.
translations.idiomatic: General Ning Shuo Jie Jin, King of Mianzhong, who has long served the state with distinguished military merit, is appointed acting General Who Wins the Championship, Commander-in-Chief, and King of Duhan.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍、八中侯餘古，弱冠輔佐，忠効夙著，今假行寧朔將軍、阿錯王。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might, Marquis of Bazhong Yu Gu, assisting since his capping years with loyalty and efficacy renowned from of old, is now granted acting General Ning Shuo and King of Acuo.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Yu Gu, Marquis of Bazhong, who has served loyally since youth, is appointed acting General Ning Shuo and King of Acuo.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍餘歷，忠款有素，文武列顯，今假行龍驤將軍、邁盧王。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Yu Li, with loyal sincerity of long standing and civil and martial merits arrayed in prominence, is now granted acting General of the Dragon Cavalry and King of Mailu.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Yu Li, long noted for loyal service and civil and martial distinction, is appointed acting General of the Dragon Cavalry and King of Mailu.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍餘固，忠効時務，光宣國政，今假行建威將軍、弗斯侯。」

translations.literal: General of Broad Might Yu Gu, loyal and effective in the affairs of the age, spreading and proclaiming the policies of state, is now granted acting General Who Establishes Might and Marquis of Fusi.'
translations.idiomatic: General of Broad Might Yu Gu, loyal in state service and a credit to government, is appointed acting General Who Establishes Might and Marquis of Fusi.'

sentences.zh: 牟大又表曰：「臣所遣行建威將軍、廣陽太守、兼長史臣高達，行建威將軍、朝鮮太守、兼司馬臣楊茂，行宣威將軍、兼參軍臣會邁等三人，志行清亮，忠款夙著。

translations.literal: Mou Da again memorialized, saying: 'The acting General Who Establishes Might, Administrator of Guangyang, and concurrent Chief Clerk, subject Gao Da; the acting General Who Establishes Might, Administrator of Chaoxian, and concurrent Major, subject Yang Mao; and the acting General Who Proclaims Might and concurrent Major, subject Hui Mai—these three men—have wills and conduct pure and bright, with loyal sincerity renowned from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Da memorialized again: 'The three envoys I sent—acting General Who Establishes Might Gao Da, Administrator of Guangyang and concurrent Chief Clerk; acting General Who Establishes Might Yang Mao, Administrator of Chaoxian and concurrent Major; and acting General Who Proclaims Might Hui Mai, concurrent Major—are men of clear integrity and long-proven loyalty.

sentences.zh: 往泰始中，比使宋朝，今任臣使，冒涉波險，尋其至効，宜在進爵，謹依先例，各假行職。

translations.literal: In the past, in Taishi, they were envoys to the Song court; now charged as my envoys, they braved waves and peril; considering their utmost efficacy, advancement in rank is fitting; respectfully, according to precedent, each is granted an acting post.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era they served as envoys to the Song court; now, bearing my commission across dangerous seas, their achievements warrant promotion; I therefore grant each an acting appointment according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 且玄澤靈休，萬里所企，況親趾天庭，乃不蒙賴。

translations.literal: Moreover, the dark grace and numinous blessing are what ten thousand li look up to; how much more when they set foot in person at the Celestial Court, yet do not receive favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your numinous grace is what men ten thousand li away look to; how much less should those who have come in person to the Celestial Court go unrewarded?

sentences.zh: 伏願天監特愍除正。

translations.literal: I bow and hope the celestial regard will specially show compassion and confirm their appointments.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Heaven's regard to confirm these appointments.

sentences.zh: 達邊効夙著，勤勞公務，今假行龍驤將軍、帶方太守。

translations.literal: Da, with border efficacy renowned from of old and diligent toil in public affairs, is now granted acting General of the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Da, long distinguished on the frontier and diligent in public service, is appointed acting General of the Dragon Cavalry and Administrator of Daifang.

sentences.zh: 茂志行清壹，公務不廢，今假行建威將軍、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Mao's will and conduct are pure and unified; public affairs are not neglected; he is now granted acting General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mao, upright in conduct and unfailing in public duty, is appointed acting General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Guangling.

translations.literal: Corrupt: wan.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔邁〕執志周密，屢致勤効，今假行廣武將軍、清河太守。」

translations.literal: [Supplied: Mai], holding his will tight and thorough, repeatedly achieving diligent efficacy, is now granted acting General of Broad Might and Administrator of Qinghe.'
translations.idiomatic: Hui Mai, steadfast and thorough in purpose and repeatedly diligent in service, is appointed acting General of Broad Might and Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 詔可，竝賜軍號，除太守。

translations.literal: An edict approved, and military titles were bestowed together with appointment as administrators.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved; military titles and prefectural appointments were granted together.

sentences.zh: 為使持節、都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Baekje, and Grand General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Baekje, and Grand General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 使兼謁者僕射孫副策命大襲亡祖父牟都為百濟王。

translations.literal: The envoy, Concurrent Master of Ceremonies Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Fu, by written mandate invested Mou Da's deceased grandfather Mou Du as King of Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy and Concurrent Master of Ceremonies Sun Fu issued the written mandate investing Mou Da's late grandfather Mou Du as King of Baekje.

sentences.zh: 曰：「於戲！

translations.literal: It said: 'Alas!
translations.idiomatic: It read: 'Ah!

sentences.zh: 惟爾世襲忠懃，誠著遐表，滄路肅澄，要貢無替。

translations.literal: Only you, inheriting loyalty and diligence through generations, with sincerity manifest on distant registers, the blue roads solemn and clear, essential tribute without lapse.
translations.idiomatic: You who have inherited loyalty through generations, whose sincerity shines to distant lands, whose sea routes lie peaceful and whose tribute never fails—

sentences.zh: 式循彝典，用纂顯命。

translations.literal: Following the constant canon, we employ you to continue the illustrious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: following the eternal canon, we invest you with the illustrious mandate.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go—revere it!
translations.idiomatic: Go, and hold it in reverence!

sentences.zh: 其敬膺休業，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Reverently receive this blessed enterprise—can you not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Receive this blessed charge with reverence—can you do otherwise?

sentences.zh: 制詔行都督百濟諸軍事、鎮東大將軍百濟王牟大今以大襲祖父牟都為百濟王，即位章綬等玉銅虎竹符四。

translations.literal: Imperial written mandate to Mou Da, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Baekje military affairs, Grand General Who Guards the East and King of Baekje: Now, by great succession, your grandfather Mou Du is made King of Baekje, with investiture seal-cord and the like, four jade, bronze, tiger, and bamboo tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mandate to Mou Da, Commander-in-Chief of Baekje and King of Baekje: By right of great succession your grandfather Mou Du is invested as King of Baekje, with regalia of seal and cord and four tallies of jade, bronze, tiger, and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 〔王〕其拜受，不亦休乎！」

translations.literal: [Supplied: King], bow and receive—is this not felicity!'
translations.idiomatic: King, bow and receive—is this not a glorious blessing!'

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏虜又發騎數十萬攻百濟，入其界，牟大遣將沙法名、贊首流、解禮昆、木干那率眾襲擊虜軍，大破之。

translations.literal: That year, the Wei barbarians again sent several hundred thousand horsemen to attack Baekje and entered its borders; Mou Da sent the generals Shafaming, Zanshouliu, Jielikun, and Muganna at the head of the masses to strike the barbarian army and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That year Northern Wei sent several hundred thousand cavalry against Baekje and crossed its border; Mou Da sent Shafaming, Zanshouliu, Jielikun, and Muganna at the head of his troops to ambush the Wei army and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，牟大遣使上表曰：「臣自昔受封，世被朝榮，忝荷節鉞，剋攘列辟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Mou Da sent envoys with a memorial, saying: 'Your subject, from of old receiving enfeoffment, has through generations received court glory, humbly bearing staff and battle-axe, overcoming and driving off the array of rivals.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 2 Mou Da sent a memorial through his envoys: 'From the time I first received investiture my house has enjoyed the court's favor; bearing your staff of command, I have beaten back rival powers.

sentences.zh: 往姐瑾等竝蒙光除，臣庶咸泰。

translations.literal: In the past Jie Jin and the rest all received brilliant appointments; subjects and commoners alike were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie Jin and the others were honored with appointments before, my people all rejoiced in peace.

sentences.zh: 去庚午年，獫狁弗悛，舉兵深逼。

translations.literal: In the past gengwu year, the Xianyun would not repent and raised troops pressing deep in.
translations.idiomatic: In the last gengwu year the Xianyun enemy would not relent and marched deep into our territory.

sentences.zh: 臣遣沙法名等領軍逆討，宵襲霆擊，匈梨張惶，崩若海蕩。

translations.literal: Your subject sent Shafaming and others to lead the army in counter-attack; by night they struck like thunder; the Xiongnu were alarmed and panicked, collapsing as if the sea were heaving.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Shafaming and others against them; our night assault fell like thunder, and the enemy fled in panic, collapsing like a tide in storm.

sentences.zh: 乘奔追斬，僵尸丹野。

translations.literal: Riding the rout they pursued and beheaded; corpses lay red across the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: We pursued the fleeing foe and struck them down until the fields lay red with the dead.

sentences.zh: 由是摧其銳氣，鯨暴韜凶。

translations.literal: Thus their sharp spirit was broken, and the whale-like violence hid its fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their fighting spirit was broken and their savage fury was forced to hide itself.

sentences.zh: 今邦宇謐靜，實名等之略，尋其功勳，宜在褒顯。

translations.literal: Now the realm is peaceful and quiet; it is truly Shafaming and the others' strategy; examining their merit, they should be honored and distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace, thanks chiefly to the strategy of Shafaming and his fellows; when one weighs their merit, they clearly deserve honor and reward.

sentences.zh: 今假沙法名行征虜將軍、邁羅王，贊首流為行安國將軍、辟中王，解禮昆為行武威將軍、弗中侯，木干那前有軍功，又拔臺舫，為行廣威將軍、面中侯。

translations.literal: Now provisionally appoint Shafaming Acting General Who Conquers the Barbarians and King of Mailuo; Zanshouliu as Acting General Who Pacifies the State and King of Bizhong; Jielikun as Acting General of Martial Prestige and Marquis of Fuzhong; and Muganna, who had previous military merit and also captured the platform fort, as Acting General of Broad Prestige and Marquis of Mianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore propose provisional titles: Shafaming as Acting General Who Conquers the Barbarians and King of Mailuo; Zanshouliu as Acting General Who Pacifies the State and King of Bizhong; Jielikun as Acting General of Martial Prestige and Marquis of Fuzhong; and Muganna, who had already distinguished himself in battle and also took the platform fort, as Acting General of Broad Prestige and Marquis of Mianzhong.

sentences.zh: 伏願天恩特愍聽除。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray Heaven's grace will specially pity and grant the appointments.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Heaven's grace may look upon them with special favor and confirm these appointments.'

sentences.zh: 又表曰：「臣所遣行龍驤將軍、樂浪太守兼長史臣慕遺，行建武將軍、城陽太守兼司馬臣王茂，兼參軍、行振武將軍、朝鮮太守臣張塞，行揚武將軍陳明，在官忘私，唯公是務，見危授命，蹈難弗顧。

translations.literal: Another memorial said: 'The envoys your subject dispatched—Acting Dragon Cavalry General, Administrator of Lelang and concurrent Chief Clerk Mu Yi; Acting General Who Establishes Martiality, Administrator of Chengyang and concurrent Grand Marshal Wang Mao; Concurrent Army Aide, Acting General Who Shakes the Barbarians, Administrator of Chaoxian Zhang Sai; and Acting General Who Raises the Martial Chen Ming—forgot private interest in office, devoted solely to public duty, accepting death in danger, treading hardship without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: 'The envoys I sent—Mu Yi, Acting Dragon Cavalry General and Administrator of Lelang, who also served as chief clerk; Wang Mao, Acting General Who Establishes Martiality and Administrator of Chengyang, who also served as grand marshal; Zhang Sai, army aide, Acting General Who Shakes the Barbarians, and Administrator of Chaoxian; and Chen Ming, Acting General Who Raises the Martial—have all served without thought of private gain, devoted only to the public good, ready to give their lives in peril and to face hardship without flinching.

sentences.zh: 今任臣使，冒涉波險，盡其至誠。

translations.literal: Now entrusted with your subject's mission, they braved waves and peril, giving their utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Now charged with my mission, they have braved the dangers of wind and sea and given themselves to it with complete sincerity.

sentences.zh: 實宜進爵，各假行署。

translations.literal: They truly deserve advancement in rank; each should receive a provisional acting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: They truly deserve promotion in rank, each with a provisional appointment.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖朝特賜除正。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray the sacred court will specially grant their formal confirmation.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray the sacred court will confirm their appointments in full.'

sentences.zh: 詔可，竝賜軍號。

translations.literal: The edict approved, and military titles were all conferred.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the request, and military titles were conferred on them all.

sentences.zh: 加羅國

translations.literal: The State of Kara.
translations.idiomatic: The State of Kara

sentences.zh: 加羅國，三韓種也。

translations.literal: The State of Kara is of the Samhan stock.
translations.idiomatic: The State of Kara belongs to the Samhan peoples.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，國王荷知使來獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, King Hezhi of the state sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 King Hezhi of Kara sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「量廣始登，遠夷洽化。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'The measure of the realm is broad; [the sovereign] has just ascended. Distant barbarians align with transformation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 'As the new reign begins, distant peoples are drawn into civilization.

sentences.zh: 加羅王荷知款關海外，奉贄東遐。

translations.literal: King Hezhi of Kara opened the frontier beyond the seas in earnest allegiance, bringing tribute from the far east.
translations.idiomatic: King Hezhi of Kara has come in sincere allegiance from beyond the sea, bearing tribute from the eastern reaches.

sentences.zh: 可授輔國將軍、本國王。」

translations.literal: He may be granted General Who Assists the State and King of his own country.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be invested as General Who Assists the State and King of his own country.'

sentences.zh: 倭國

translations.literal: The State of Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Wa

sentences.zh: 倭國，在帶方東南大海㠀中。

translations.literal: Wa lies on an island in the great sea southeast of Daifang.
translations.idiomatic: Wa lies on an island in the open sea southeast of Daifang.

sentences.zh: 漢末以來立女王。

translations.literal: Since the end of Han they have had a queen as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Since the end of the Han dynasty they have been ruled by queens.

sentences.zh: 土俗已見前史。

translations.literal: Local customs are already recorded in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs are already described in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，進新除使持節、都督倭新羅任那加羅秦韓六國諸軍事、安東大將軍、倭王武號爲鎭東大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the newly appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for the six states of Wa, Silla, Mimana, Kara, and Jinhan, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, King Bu of Wa, was promoted to Grand General Who Garrisons the East.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 the court promoted the newly appointed King Bu of Wa—Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief over Wa, Silla, Mimana, Kara, and Jinhan, and Grand General Who Pacifies the East—to Grand General Who Garrisons the East.

sentences.zh: 南夷

translations.literal: Southern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Yi

sentences.zh: 南夷林邑國，在交州南，海行三千里，北連九德，秦時故林邑縣也。

translations.literal: The Southern Yi state of Linyi lies south of Jiaozhou, three thousand li by sea; to the north it adjoins Jiude; it was the former Linyi county of Qin times.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Southern Yi, the state of Linyi lies south of Jiaozhou, three thousand li by sea; to the north it borders Jiude, and in Qin times it had been Linyi county.

sentences.zh: 漢末稱王。

translations.literal: At the end of Han it styled itself a kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Han it began calling itself a kingdom.

sentences.zh: 晉太康五年，始貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taikang of Jin it first sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taikang year 5 it first sent tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 宋永初元年，林邑王范楊邁初產，母夢人以金席藉之，光色奇麗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu of Song, when Fan Yangmai, king of Linyi, was born, his mother dreamed that someone spread a golden mat beneath him, its light and color wondrously beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yongchu year 1, when King Fan Yangmai of Linyi was born, his mother dreamed that a figure spread a golden mat beneath him, radiant and strangely beautiful.

sentences.zh: 中國謂紫磨金，夷人謂之「楊邁」，故以為名。

translations.literal: The Central States call it purple-refined gold; the barbarians call it 'Yangmai,' hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese call that kind of gold purple-refined gold; the locals call it 'Yangmai,' and so he was named.

sentences.zh: 楊邁死，子咄立，慕其父，復改名楊邁。

translations.literal: When Yangmai died, his son Duo ascended the throne; adoring his father, he again took the name Yangmai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangmai died, his son Duo succeeded him; out of devotion to his father, he too took the name Yangmai.

sentences.zh: 林邑有金山，金汁流出於浦。

translations.literal: Linyi has a Gold Mountain; liquid gold flows out at the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi has a Gold Mountain from which molten gold runs out onto the beach.

sentences.zh: 事尼乾道，鑄金銀人像，大十圍。

translations.literal: They follow the Nirgrantha way, casting gold and silver human images ten arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: They follow the Nirgrantha faith and cast gold and silver human images ten arm-spans in girth.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，交州刺史檀和之伐林邑，楊邁欲輸金萬斤，銀十萬斤，銅三十萬斤，還日南地。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, Inspector Tan Hezhi of Jiaozhou attacked Linyi; Yangmai wished to surrender ten thousand jin of gold, one hundred thousand jin of silver, three hundred thousand jin of copper, and return the land of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 22 Inspector Tan Hezhi of Jiaozhou invaded Linyi; Yangmai offered to surrender ten thousand jin of gold, one hundred thousand jin of silver, and three hundred thousand jin of copper, and to restore the territory of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 大臣䓯僧達諫，不聽。

translations.literal: The minister Fan Shingda remonstrated; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The minister Fan Shingda urged against it, but Yangmai would not listen.

sentences.zh: 和之進兵破其北界犬戎區栗城，獲金寶無笇，毀其金人，得黃金數萬斤，餘物稱是。

translations.literal: Hezhi advanced and broke their northern border Dog Rong city Qulicheng, captured incalculable gold and treasure, destroyed their golden statues, obtained tens of thousands of jin of gold, and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi pressed forward and took Qulicheng on their northern frontier; the booty in gold and jewels was beyond counting. He destroyed their golden images, seized tens of thousands of jin of gold, and carried off comparable stores of everything else.

sentences.zh: 和之後病死，見胡神為祟。

translations.literal: Afterwards Hezhi died of illness; he was seen to be haunted by the foreign god.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi later died of illness; people said the foreign god he had desecrated was tormenting him.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，始以林邑長史范龍跋為揚武將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, Fan Longba, chief clerk of Linyi, was first made General Who Raises the Martial.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year 2 Fan Longba, chief clerk of Linyi, was first appointed General Who Raises the Martial.

sentences.zh: 楊邁子孫相傳為王，未有位號。

translations.literal: Yangmai's descendants succeeded one another as kings without established titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yangmai's line continued to rule in succession, but without formal titles from the court.

sentences.zh: 夷人范當根純攻奪其國，篡立為王。

translations.literal: The barbarian Fan Danggenchun attacked and seized the country, usurping the throne as king.
translations.idiomatic: The local chieftain Fan Danggenchun seized the realm by force and installed himself as king.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，遣使貢獻金簟等物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, he sent envoys presenting tribute of golden mats and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 9 he sent envoys with tribute, including golden mats and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「林邑

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Linyi
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 'Linyi

translations.literal: Corrupt: chong.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔雖〕介在遐外，世服王化。

translations.literal: Though remote beyond the borders, for generations they have submitted to royal civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Though it lies far beyond the frontier, it has for generations accepted the court's civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 當根純乃誠款到，率其僚職，遠績克宣，良有可嘉。

translations.literal: Danggenchun has shown sincere allegiance, leading his officials; his distant achievement is well fulfilled—truly commendable.
translations.idiomatic: Danggenchun has come in sincere allegiance at the head of his officials; his loyal service from afar deserves real praise.

sentences.zh: 宜沾爵號，以弘休澤。

translations.literal: He should receive enfeoffment and title to extend imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: He should be granted rank and title so that imperial favor may reach him.

sentences.zh: 可持節、都督緣海諸軍事、安南將軍、林邑王。」

translations.literal: He may be granted Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of coastal military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of coastal military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.'

sentences.zh: 范楊邁子孫范諸農率種人攻當根純，復得本國。

translations.literal: Fan Zhunong, descendant of Fan Yangmai, led his tribesmen to attack Danggenchun and recovered their homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhunong, a descendant of Fan Yangmai, rallied his people against Danggenchun and won back the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 十年，以諸農為持節、都督緣海諸軍事、安南將軍、林邑王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Zhunong was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of coastal affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Zhunong was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of coastal military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to Grand General Who Garrisons the South.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 2 his title was raised to Grand General Who Garrisons the South.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，諸農入朝，海中遭風溺死，以其子文款為假節、都督緣海軍事、安南將軍、林邑王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Zhunong came to court, drowned in a storm at sea; his son Wenkuan was made Provisional Bearer of the Staff, Commander of coastal military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai year 1 Zhunong came to court but drowned in a storm at sea; his son Wenkuan was appointed Provisional Bearer of the Staff, Commander of coastal military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, and King of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 晉建興中，日南夷帥范稚奴文數商賈，見上國制度，教林邑王范逸起城池樓殿。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing era of Jin, the Rinan Yi chieftain Fan Zhinu, having traded on numerous occasions, saw the institutions of the superior state and taught King Fanyi of Linyi to build walls, towers, and halls.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin's Jianxing era the Rinan chieftain Fan Zhinu, who had traveled many times as a merchant, saw how the central realm was governed and taught King Fan Yi of Linyi to raise city walls, towers, and palaces.

sentences.zh: 王服天冠如佛冠，身被香纓絡。

translations.literal: The king wears a heavenly crown like a Buddhist crown, his body draped in fragrant jewel chains.
translations.idiomatic: The king wears a celestial crown shaped like a Buddhist crown and drapes himself in fragrant strings of jewels.

sentences.zh: 國人凶悍，習山川，善鬬。

translations.literal: The people are fierce, know the mountains and rivers, and are skilled at fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The people are fierce, know every hill and stream, and fight well.

sentences.zh: 吹海蠡為角。

translations.literal: They blow sea conchs as horns.
translations.idiomatic: They use sea conchs as war horns.

sentences.zh: 人皆裸露。

translations.literal: The people all go naked.
translations.idiomatic: The people go about naked.

sentences.zh: 四時暄暖，無霜雪。

translations.literal: All four seasons are warm; there is no frost or snow.
translations.idiomatic: All four seasons are warm, and there is neither frost nor snow.

sentences.zh: 貴女賤男，謂師君為婆羅門。

translations.literal: They esteem women and slight men; they call teachers and lords 'Brahman.'
translations.idiomatic: Women are honored and men are held lightly; teachers and rulers are called Brahmans.

sentences.zh: 羣從相姻通，婦先遣娉求婿。

translations.literal: Clansmen intermarry; the woman first sends betrothal gifts to seek a husband.
translations.idiomatic: Clans intermarry, and it is the woman who first sends betrothal gifts to choose a husband.

sentences.zh: 女嫁者，迦藍衣橫幅合縫如井闌，首戴花寶。

translations.literal: When women marry, they wear kāla cloth in horizontal panels sewn together like a well-curb, their heads crowned with flowered jewels.
translations.idiomatic: A bride wears kāla cloth cut in horizontal panels and sewn together like a well-curb, with flowers and jewels on her head.

sentences.zh: 婆羅門牽婿與婦握手相付，呪願吉利。

translations.literal: A Brahman leads groom and bride, joining their hands in transfer, chanting blessings for good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: A Brahman joins the groom's and bride's hands and chants blessings for good fortune.

sentences.zh: 居喪剪髮，謂之孝。

translations.literal: In mourning they cut their hair, calling it filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning they cut their hair, which they call filial duty.

sentences.zh: 燔尸中野以為葬。

translations.literal: They burn corpses in the open wild as burial.
translations.idiomatic: They burn the dead in the open country as burial.

sentences.zh: 遠界有靈鷲鳥，知人將死，集其家食死人肉盡，飛去，乃取骨燒灰投海中水葬。

translations.literal: At the far borders there are sacred vulture birds; knowing when someone will die, they gather at the household, eat the dead flesh to the last, fly away; then the bones are taken, burned to ash, and cast into the sea as water burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the remote borderlands there are sacred vultures that know when a person is about to die. They gather at the house, devour the corpse, and fly away; then the bones are burned to ash and cast into the sea in a water burial.

sentences.zh: 人色以黑為美，南方諸國皆然。

translations.literal: Among the people black skin is considered beautiful; all southern states are alike in this.
translations.idiomatic: Dark skin is considered beautiful there, as it is throughout the southern kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 區栗城建八尺表，日影度南八寸。

translations.literal: At Qulicheng they set up an eight-foot gnomon; the shadow at noon points south eight inches.
translations.idiomatic: At Qulicheng they erected an eight-foot gnomon; at noon the shadow falls eight inches to the south.

sentences.zh: 自林邑西南三千餘里，至扶南。

translations.literal: From Linyi, three thousand-odd li to the southwest, one reaches Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand-odd li southwest of Linyi lies Funan.

sentences.zh: 扶南國，在日南之南大海西

translations.literal: The state of Funan, west of the great sea south of Rinan
translations.idiomatic: The state of Funan lies west of the great sea south of Rinan

translations.literal: Corrupt: man.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔灣〕中，廣袤三千餘里，有大江水西流入海。

translations.literal: In the gulf, extending three thousand-odd li; a great river flows west into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In a gulf more than three thousand li across, a great river runs westward into the sea.

sentences.zh: 其先有女人為王，名柳葉。

translations.literal: Formerly a woman was king, named Liuye.
translations.idiomatic: In earliest times a woman ruled as queen; her name was Liuye.

sentences.zh: 又有激國人混填，夢神賜弓一張，教乘舶入海。

translations.literal: Also there was Hun Tian from the state of Ji; he dreamed the god gave him a bow and instructed him to take a ship to sea.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Hun Tian of the state of Ji, who dreamed that a god gave him a bow and told him to put to sea.

sentences.zh: 混填晨起於神廟樹下得弓，即乘舶向扶南。

translations.literal: Hun Tian rose early and found the bow beneath a tree at the god's shrine; he immediately took ship toward Funan.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Tian rose at dawn, found the bow under a tree at the god's shrine, and at once sailed for Funan.

sentences.zh: 柳葉見舶，率眾欲禦之。

translations.literal: Liuye saw the ship and led the masses intending to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Liuye saw the ship, she gathered her people to drive it off.

sentences.zh: 混填舉弓遙射，貫船一面通中人。

translations.literal: Hun Tian raised his bow and shot from afar; it pierced clean through one side of the ship.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Tian drew his bow and shot from a distance, sending an arrow clear through one side of the vessel.

sentences.zh: 柳葉怖，遂降。

translations.literal: Liuye was frightened and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Liuye surrendered.

sentences.zh: 混填娶以為妻。

translations.literal: Hun Tian took her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Tian married her.

sentences.zh: 惡其裸露形體，乃疊布貫其首。

translations.literal: Disliking their naked bodies, he layered cloth and passed it through their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Disliking their nakedness, he had them wrap layered cloth around their bodies.

sentences.zh: 遂治其國。

translations.literal: Thereupon he governed the country.
translations.idiomatic: He then ruled the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 子孫相傳。

translations.literal: Descendants succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: His line ruled in succession.

sentences.zh: 至王槃況死，國人立其大將范師蔓。

translations.literal: When King Pan Kuang died, the people installed his great general Fan Shiman.
translations.idiomatic: When King Pan Kuang died, the people raised his chief general Fan Shiman to the throne.

sentences.zh: 蔓病，姊子旃

translations.literal: Shiman fell ill; his sister's son Zhan
translations.idiomatic: When Shiman fell ill, his sister's son Zhan

translations.literal: Corrupt: mu.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔篡〕立，殺蔓子金生。

translations.literal: He usurped the throne and killed Shiman's son Jinsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the throne by force and killed Shiman's son Jinsheng.

sentences.zh: 十餘年，蔓少子長襲殺旃，以刃鑱旃腹曰：「汝昔殺我兄，今為父兄報汝。」

translations.literal: After more than ten years, Shiman's youngest son Changxi killed Zhan, thrusting a blade into Zhan's belly and saying: 'You once killed my elder brother; now I repay you for father and brother.'
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later Shiman's youngest son Changxi killed Zhan, driving a blade into his belly and saying, 'You killed my elder brother; now I avenge my father and brother.'

sentences.zh: 旃大將范尋又殺長，國人立以為王，是吳、晉時也。

translations.literal: Zhan's general Fan Xun then killed Changxi; the people installed him as king—this was in the Wu and Jin era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's general Fan Xun then killed Changxi, and the people made Fan Xun king—this was in the Wu and Jin period.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋世通職貢。

translations.literal: In Jin and Song times they regularly sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin and Song it sent regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 宋末，扶南王姓僑陳如，名闍耶跋摩，遣商貨至廣州。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, the Funan king, surname Kau Chenru, name Jayavarman, sent merchants to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Song the Funan king, of the Kau Chenru clan and named Jayavarman, sent traders to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 天竺道人那伽仙附載欲歸國，遭風至林邑，掠其財物皆盡。

translations.literal: The Indian monk Nagasena took passage intending to return home; caught by wind at Linyi, his goods were plundered entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The Indian monk Nagasena took passage on the ship intending to return home, but was blown by storm to Linyi, where his goods were plundered to the last item.

sentences.zh: 那伽仙閒道得達扶南，具說中國有聖主受命。

translations.literal: Nagasena found a route and reached Funan, fully recounting that China had a sage sovereign receiving the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Nagasena found his way to Funan and told at length how China had a sage ruler who had received Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，闍耶跋摩遣天竺道人釋那伽仙上表稱扶南國王臣僑陳如闍耶跋摩叩頭啟曰：「天化撫育，感動靈祇，四氣調適。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming, Jayavarman sent the Indian monk Shizi Nagasena with a memorial, saying 'King of Funan, your subject Kau Chenru Jayavarman, kowtowing, reports: Heavenly transformation nurtures and cherishes, moving the spirits; the four seasons are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 2 Jayavarman sent the Indian monk Nagasena with a memorial in which he wrote, as King of Funan and subject Kau Chenru Jayavarman, kowtowing: 'Heaven's transforming power nurtures all beneath it, moving gods and spirits; the four seasons are in balance.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖主尊體起居康

translations.literal: I humbly pray the sage sovereign's honored person, in daily rising and resting, may be healthy and
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that the sage sovereign's sacred person may rise and rest in health and

translations.literal: Corrupt: yu.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔豫〕，皇太子萬福，六宮清休，諸王妃主內外朝臣普同和睦，隣境士庶萬國歸心，五穀豐熟，災害不生，土清民泰，一切安穩。

translations.literal: At ease; the crown prince ten thousand blessings; the six palaces serene; princes and princesses inside and outside, court ministers all harmonious; neighboring lands and commoners of ten thousand states turn their hearts; five grains abundant; disasters not arising; land clear and people at peace; everything secure.
translations.idiomatic: At ease; that the crown prince may enjoy boundless fortune, the six palaces dwell in tranquility, princes and princesses within and without and all court ministers live in harmony, neighboring peoples and subjects of every land turn their hearts to you, the five grains ripen in abundance, disasters do not arise, the realm is clear and the people secure, and all is stable.

sentences.zh: 臣及人民，國土豐樂，四氣調和，道俗濟濟，竝蒙陛下光化所被，咸荷安泰。」

translations.literal: Your subject and the people, the land rich and joyous, four seasons harmonious, monks and laity thronging, all alike covered by Your Majesty's luminous transformation, all bearing peace and security.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject and my people dwell in a rich and happy land; the four seasons are harmonious; monks and laypeople flourish together—all alike under Your Majesty's radiant transforming power, and all enjoy peace and security.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣前遣使齎雜物行廣州貨易，天竺道人釋那伽仙於廣州因附臣舶欲來扶南，海中風漂到林邑，國王奪臣貨易，并那伽仙私財。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Your subject previously sent envoys bearing mixed goods to trade at Guangzhou; the Indian monk Shizi Nagasena at Guangzhou took passage on your subject's ship intending to come to Funan; wind at sea drifted them to Linyi, and the king seized your subject's trade goods and Nagasena's private property as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'I previously sent envoys with goods to trade at Guangzhou. The Indian monk Nagasena boarded my ship at Guangzhou intending to return to Funan, but wind and tide drove us to Linyi, where the king seized my merchandise and Nagasena's private property as well.

sentences.zh: 具陳其從中國來此，仰序陛下聖德仁治，詳議風化，佛法興顯，眾僧殷集，法事日盛，王威嚴整，朝望國軌，慈愍蒼生，八方六合，莫不歸伏。

translations.literal: He fully recounted coming from China, praising Your Majesty's sage virtue and benevolent governance, deliberating on culture and transformation, Buddhism flourishing, monks gathering richly, dharma affairs daily thriving, royal authority stern and ordered, court observing national norms, compassion for the living, eight directions and six quarters—none do not submit.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke at length of his journey from China, praising Your Majesty's sage virtue and humane rule, your care for customs and moral transformation, the flourishing of Buddhism, the gathering of monks, the daily growth of religious rites, the majesty and order of the throne, the dignity of court and state, and compassion for all living beings—so that in every direction under heaven none fail to submit.

sentences.zh: 如聽其所說，則化隣諸天，非可為喻。

translations.literal: If one hears what he says, the transformation reaches neighboring heavens—it cannot be expressed in comparison.
translations.idiomatic: To hear him tell it, your transforming power reaches even the heavens beyond—words cannot do it justice.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，下情踊悅，若蹔奉見尊足，仰慕慈恩，澤流小國，天垂所感，率土之民，竝得皆蒙恩祐。

translations.literal: Your subject hearing this, the lower feelings leaped with joy; if briefly permitted to see your honored feet, yearning for compassionate grace, bounty flowing to a small state—Heaven's feeling, all within the realm would equally receive gracious protection.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard this my heart leaped with joy. If I might even briefly behold your sacred presence, I would look up to your compassionate grace as a stream of bounty reaching even a small kingdom such as mine; touched by Heaven, all people within the realm would share in that blessing.

sentences.zh: 是以臣今遣此道人釋那伽仙為使，上表問訊奉貢，微獻呈臣等赤心，并別陳下情。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject now sends this monk Shizi Nagasena as envoy to present this memorial of inquiry and tribute, humbly offering to show our heartfelt loyalty, and separately stating our lower situation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I now send this monk Nagasena as my envoy to present this memorial of greeting and tribute, offering in all humility the loyalty of my heart, and separately setting forth my petition below.

sentences.zh: 但所獻輕陋，愧懼唯深。

translations.literal: But what is offered is slight and mean; shame and fear are profound alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I offer is meager and poor, and my shame and fear are very deep.

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈曲照，鑒其丹款，賜不垂責。」

translations.literal: I prostrate myself wishing Heaven's compassion to bend its illumination, examine our cinnabar sincerity, and grant that blame not be visited.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that your heavenly kindness may look upon us with favor, recognize our heartfelt loyalty, and withhold your censure.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣有奴名鳩酬羅，委臣

translations.literal: He also said: 'Your subject has a slave named Jiuchouluo, entrusted to your subject
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'I have a slave named Jiuchouluo who was entrusted to me

translations.literal: Corrupt: mian.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔逸〕走，別在餘處，構結兇逆，遂破林邑，仍自立為王。

translations.literal: fled, separated and in another place, formed wicked treason, then broke Linyi, and still set himself up as king.
translations.idiomatic: He fled and made his base elsewhere, gathered wicked rebels, overran Linyi, and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 永不恭從，違恩負義，叛主之諐，天不容載。

translations.literal: Forever not submitting respectfully, violating grace and bearing guilt against obligation, the fault of rebelling against his master—Heaven cannot bear to record him.
translations.idiomatic: He never submits in respect, repays kindness with betrayal, and rebels against his master—a crime Heaven itself cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 伏尋林邑昔為檀和之所破，久已歸化。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and reflect: Linyi was once broken by Tan Hezhi and long since submitted to civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the past, Linyi was once conquered by Tan Hezhi and had long accepted the court's rule.

sentences.zh: 天威所被，四海彌伏，而今鳩酬羅守執奴兇，自專很彊。

translations.literal: Where Heaven's might reaches, the four seas all submit; yet now Jiuchouluo holds to his slave wickedness, self-willed and fiercely strong.
translations.idiomatic: Where your heavenly might reaches, all within the four seas submits—yet Jiuchouluo clings to his rebellious defiance and acts with brutal arrogance on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 且林邑扶南隣界相接，親又是臣奴，猶尚逆去，朝廷遙遠，豈復遵奉。

translations.literal: Moreover Linyi and Funan share adjoining borders; he is personally again your subject's slave, yet still turned rebellious; the court is far—how could they again observe submission?
translations.idiomatic: Linyi borders my own kingdom of Funan, and he is my own former slave—yet even he turned rebel. If the court is so remote, how can such lands be expected to remain loyal?

sentences.zh: 此國屬陛下，故謹具上啟。

translations.literal: This state belongs to Your Majesty; therefore I respectfully present this full report.
translations.idiomatic: This kingdom belongs to Your Majesty, and therefore I respectfully submit this full account.

sentences.zh: 伏聞林邑頃年表獻簡絕，便欲永隔朝廷，豈有師子坐而安大鼠。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and have heard that Linyi in recent years has ceased memorial tribute, wishing to cut off from the court forever—can a lion sit at ease while a great rat does so?
translations.idiomatic: I understand that Linyi has recently cut off its tributary gifts and seeks to sever ties with the court forever—can a lion sit idle while a mere rat grows bold?

sentences.zh: 伏願遣軍將伐兇逆，臣亦自効微誠，助朝廷剪撲，使邊海諸國，一時歸伏。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself wishing you would send generals to attack the wicked rebels; your subject will also offer his slight sincerity, aiding the court in cutting them down, so that all the border-sea states at once submit.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that you send troops against these rebels; I shall offer what little loyalty I can to help the court destroy them, so that all the kingdoms along the southern seas may submit at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下若欲別立餘人為彼王者，伏聽勑旨。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to install another person as their king, I prostrate myself and await your command.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to install someone else as king there, I await your decree.

sentences.zh: 脫未欲灼然興兵伐林邑者，伏願特賜勑在所，隨宜以少軍助臣，乘天之威，殄滅小賊，伐惡從善。

translations.literal: If you are not yet willing to openly raise troops against Linyi, I prostrate myself wishing you would specially grant decree to the local authorities to assist your subject with a modest force as appropriate, riding Heaven's might to exterminate the petty bandits, punishing evil and following good.
translations.idiomatic: If you are not yet ready to launch a full campaign against Linyi, I beg you at least to instruct the local authorities to send a small force to aid me, so that under Heaven's aweful might we may wipe out these petty rebels and restore righteousness.

sentences.zh: 平蕩之日，上表獻金五婆羅。

translations.literal: On the day of pacification, I will present a memorial offering five patalas of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the land is pacified, I shall submit a memorial tribute of five patalas of gold.

sentences.zh: 今輕此使送臣丹誠，表所陳啟，不盡下情。

translations.literal: Now I lightly send this envoy to convey your subject's cinnabar sincerity; the matters stated in the memorial do not fully express our lower sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: I now send this humble envoy to convey my heartfelt loyalty; the memorial above cannot fully express all that I wish to say.

sentences.zh: 謹附那伽仙并其伴口具啟聞。

translations.literal: I respectfully append Nagasena and his companions to report orally in full.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully attach Nagasena and his companions, who will report the full details orally.

sentences.zh: 伏願愍所啟。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself wishing compassion for what is reported.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg you to look with compassion upon my petition.

sentences.zh: 并獻金鏤龍王坐像一軀，白檀像一軀，牙塔二軀，古貝二雙，瑠璃蘇鉝二口，瑇瑁檳榔柈一枚。」

translations.literal: Also offering one gilded golden seated image of the Dragon King, one white sandalwood image, two ivory pagodas, two pairs of ancient cowrie shells, two mouths of glass vessels, and one tortoiseshell betel tray.'
translations.idiomatic: I also present one gilded golden seated image of the Dragon King, one white sandalwood Buddha image, two ivory pagodas, two pairs of cowrie shells, two glass vessels, and one tortoiseshell betel tray.'

sentences.zh: 那伽仙詣京師，言其國俗事摩䤈首羅天神，神常降於摩躭山。

translations.literal: Nagasena came to the capital and said that in his country's custom they worship Mahesvara god; the god regularly descends on Mount Modu.
translations.idiomatic: Nagasena traveled to the capital and reported that his people worship the god Mahesvara, who regularly descends upon Mount Modu.

sentences.zh: 土氣恒暖，草木不落。

translations.literal: The soil's qi is always warm; grasses and trees do not fall.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is always warm, and the trees never lose their leaves.

sentences.zh: 其上書曰：「吉祥利世閒，感攝於羣生。

translations.literal: His written submission says: 'Auspicious and benefiting the world, touching and gathering all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: His written submission reads: 'Blessed and bringing good to the world, drawing all living beings to your grace.

sentences.zh: 所以其然者，天感化緣明。

translations.literal: The reason it is so: Heaven's transforming influence and karmic conditions are clear.
translations.idiomatic: This is so because Heaven's transforming power and the bonds of fate are manifest.

sentences.zh: 仙山名摩躭，吉樹敷嘉榮。

translations.literal: The immortal mountain is named Modu; auspicious trees spread fine glory.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred mountain is called Modu; blessed trees flourish there in splendor.

sentences.zh: 摩䤈首羅天，依此降尊靈。

translations.literal: Mahesvara Heaven, relying on this descends in honored spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The god Mahesvara descends here in his sacred presence.

sentences.zh: 國土悉蒙祐，人民皆安寧。

translations.literal: The land entirely receives blessing; the people all have peace.
translations.idiomatic: The whole land is blessed, and the people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 由斯恩被故，是以臣歸情。

translations.literal: Because of this grace being extended, therefore your subject turns his heart in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Because we have received this grace, I now turn my heart in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 菩薩行忍慈，本迹起凡基。

translations.literal: The bodhisattva practices forbearance and compassion; root traces rise from a worldly foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The bodhisattva walks in patience and compassion, rising from ordinary human beginnings.

sentences.zh: 一發菩提心，二乘非所期。

translations.literal: Once arousing the bodhi mind, the two vehicles are not what is sought.
translations.idiomatic: Once the mind of enlightenment is awakened, the lesser paths of the two vehicles are no longer sought.

sentences.zh: 歷生積功業，六度行大悲。

translations.literal: Through lives accumulating merit, the six perfections practice great compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Through life after life he accumulated merit, practicing the six perfections in boundless compassion.

sentences.zh: 勇猛超劫數，財命捨無遺。

translations.literal: Bold and brave surpassing kalpas, wealth and life cast away without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: With courage surpassing countless ages, he gave away wealth and life without reserve.

sentences.zh: 生死不為猒，六道化有緣。

translations.literal: Birth and death are not loathed; the six paths of transformation have karmic ties.
translations.idiomatic: He did not shrink from birth and death, but taught beings throughout the six realms as fate allowed.

sentences.zh: 具脩於十地，遺果度人天。

translations.literal: Fully cultivating the ten stages, leaving fruits to ferry humans and gods.
translations.idiomatic: Having fully traversed the ten bodhisattva stages, he left the fruit of salvation for gods and mortals alike.

sentences.zh: 功業既已定，行滿登正覺。

translations.literal: Merit and work already settled, practice full he ascends to right awakening.
translations.idiomatic: When his work was complete and his practice fulfilled, he attained perfect enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 萬善智圓備，惠日照塵俗。

translations.literal: Ten thousand good acts, wisdom complete and prepared; the grace sun shines on dusty custom.
translations.idiomatic: All virtues and wisdom complete, his merciful sun shines upon a world sunk in dust.

sentences.zh: 眾生感緣應，隨機授法藥。

translations.literal: Living beings respond to felt karmic ties; according to capacity he bestows the dharma medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When beings responded to his call, he gave each the medicine of the Law as their needs required.

sentences.zh: 佛化遍十方，無不蒙濟擢。

translations.literal: Buddha's transformation fills the ten directions; none fail to receive rescue and uplift.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha's teaching reaches every quarter of the world, and none are left without salvation.

sentences.zh: 皇帝聖弘道，興隆於三寶。

translations.literal: The Emperor sage, broadly proclaiming the Way, flourishing the Three Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, sage in the Way, causes the Three Treasures to flourish.

sentences.zh: 垂心覽萬機，威恩振八表。

translations.literal: Bending his heart to survey the myriad affairs; authority and grace shake the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: He bends his mind to the myriad affairs of state; his majesty and kindness reach to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 國土及城邑，仁風化清皎。

translations.literal: States and cities—benevolent winds transform them clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Through realm and city alike, his humane influence shines clear and pure.

sentences.zh: 亦如釋提洹，眾天中最超。

translations.literal: Also like Sakra, among all heavens most surpassing.
translations.idiomatic: Even as Sakra surpasses all other gods,

sentences.zh: 陛下臨萬民，四海共歸心，聖慈流無疆，被臣小國深。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty oversees the myriad people; the four seas together turn their hearts; sage compassion flows without bounds, covering your subject's small state deeply.'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules all peoples; the four seas turn their hearts to you; your sage compassion knows no bounds and reaches even my little kingdom deeply.'

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「具摩䤈降靈，流施彼土，雖殊俗異化，遙深欣讚。

translations.literal: The edict in reply said: 'Fully the Mahesvara spirit descends, flowing and spreading in that land—though customs differ and transformation varies, from afar we deeply rejoice and praise.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply read: 'That Mahesvara's spirit descends and spreads its blessings in your land fills us with deep joy and praise, though your customs differ from ours.

sentences.zh: 知鳩酬羅於彼背叛，竊據林邑，聚兇肆掠，殊宜剪討。

translations.literal: Knowing that Jiuchouluo there rebelled, stealthily occupying Linyi, gathering villains and wantonly plundering—it is especially fitting to cut down and attack.
translations.idiomatic: We know that Jiuchouluo has rebelled there, seized Linyi by force, gathered villains, and plundered at will—such conduct clearly calls for suppression.

sentences.zh: 彼雖介遐

translations.literal: There, though remote corner
translations.idiomatic: Though it lies in a remote corner,

translations.literal: Corrupt: xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Text corrupt.

sentences.zh: 〔陬〕，舊脩蕃貢，自宋季多難，海譯致壅，皇化惟新，習迷未革。

translations.literal: Jiezhou, formerly maintained frontier tribute; since the Song era's many troubles, sea routes blocked, royal civilization newly renewed, entrenched confusion not yet reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhou once maintained tributary relations. Since the troubles of the Song years, maritime routes have been blocked; though your civilizing influence is renewed, old habits of defiance have not yet changed.

sentences.zh: 朕方以文德來遠人，未欲便興干戈。

translations.literal: I am now using civil virtue to draw distant people, not yet wishing to raise weapons immediately.
translations.idiomatic: I am now seeking to win distant peoples through civil virtue, and am not yet ready to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 王既欵列忠到，遠請軍威，今詔交部隨宜應接。

translations.literal: The King having sincerely listed his loyalty, requesting military might from afar—the command now orders Jiaozhou to respond as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Since you have shown sincere loyalty and asked from afar for military support, I now command the Jiao region to assist you as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 伐叛柔服，寔惟國典，勉立殊效，以副所期。

translations.literal: Punishing rebels and gentle submission—truly the national canon; strive to establish exceptional achievement to match what is expected.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing rebellion and winning submission by gentleness is the proper duty of state; strive to achieve outstanding results worthy of our expectations.

sentences.zh: 那伽仙屢銜邊譯，頗悉中土闊狹，令其具宣。」
