translations.literal: Nagasena repeatedly carried border interpretation and fairly knows the breadth and narrowness of the central land—have him fully declare.'
translations.idiomatic: Nagasena has often served as an interpreter on the frontier and knows the Central Plain fairly well—let him explain in full.'

sentences.zh: 上報以絳紫地黃碧綠紋綾各五匹。

translations.literal: In return from above, crimson, purple, yellow-on-purple-ground, and green patterned damasks, five bolts each.
translations.idiomatic: In reply the court sent five bolts each of crimson, purple, yellow-on-purple-ground, and green patterned damask.

sentences.zh: 扶南人黠惠知巧，攻略傍邑不賓之民為奴婢，貨易金銀綵帛。

translations.literal: The people of Funan are cunning, clever, and skilled; they attack and seize neighboring settlements' unsubmissive people as male and female slaves, trading gold, silver, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The Funanese are clever and resourceful; they raid neighboring settlements and take unsubmissive peoples as slaves, trading them for gold, silver, and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 大家男子截錦為橫幅，女為貫頭，貧者以布自蔽。

translations.literal: Great families' men cut brocade into horizontal banners; women wear tube-head garments; the poor cover themselves with cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Men of wealthy families wear brocade sashes across the chest; women wear tube-shaped head wraps; the poor cover themselves with plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 鍜金鐶鏆銀食器。

translations.literal: They forge gold rings and silver eating vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They forge gold rings and make silver tableware.

sentences.zh: 伐木起屋，國王居重閤，以木柵為城。

translations.literal: They cut timber to raise houses; the king dwells in a multi-storied pavilion; wooden palisades serve as walls.
translations.idiomatic: They cut timber to build houses; the king lives in a multi-storied hall, and wooden palisades form the city walls.

sentences.zh: 海邊生大箬葉，長八九尺，編其葉以覆屋。

translations.literal: By the sea grow great bamboo-leaves eight or nine chi long; they weave the leaves to cover houses.
translations.idiomatic: Large bamboo leaves eight or nine feet long grow by the sea; they weave these leaves to roof their houses.

sentences.zh: 人民亦為閣居。

translations.literal: The people also live in raised pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: The common people also live in raised houses.

sentences.zh: 為船八九丈，廣裁六七尺，頭尾似魚。

translations.literal: They build boats eight or nine zhang long, about six or seven chi wide, bow and stern shaped like fish.
translations.idiomatic: Their boats are eight or nine zhang long and about six or seven chi wide, with bow and stern shaped like fish.

sentences.zh: 國王行乘象，婦人亦能乘象。

translations.literal: The king when traveling rides an elephant; women also can ride elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The king travels by elephant, and women ride elephants as well.

sentences.zh: 鬪鷄及狶為樂。

translations.literal: Cockfighting and pigs serve as amusement.
translations.idiomatic: They amuse themselves with cockfighting and pig fighting.

sentences.zh: 無牢獄，有訟者，則以金指鐶若鷄子投沸湯中，令探之，又燒鎖令赤，著手上捧行七步，有罪者手皆燋爛，無罪者不傷。

translations.literal: There are no prisons; when there are lawsuits, a gold finger-ring the size of a chicken egg is thrown into boiling water and the parties are made to retrieve it; also a lock is heated red-hot, placed on the hand, and borne while walking seven steps—the guilty have hands all scorched and rotted; the innocent are not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: There are no prisons. In a lawsuit, a gold ring the size of a hen's egg is thrown into boiling water and the parties must retrieve it; or a lock is heated red-hot, placed on the hand, and carried seven paces—the guilty have their hands burned and blistered, while the innocent are unharmed.

sentences.zh: 又令沒水，直者入即不沈，不直者即沈也。

translations.literal: They also make them submerge in water—the upright enter and do not sink; the not upright sink at once.
translations.idiomatic: They also have the accused plunge into water: the innocent do not sink, while the guilty sink at once.

sentences.zh: 有甘蔗、諸蔗、安石榴及橘，多檳榔，鳥獸如中國。

translations.literal: There are sugarcane, various canes, pomegranates and oranges, many betel nuts; birds and beasts are like those of China.
translations.idiomatic: Sugarcane, various reeds, pomegranates, and oranges grow there, and betel nuts are plentiful; the birds and beasts resemble those of China.

sentences.zh: 人性善，不便戰，常為林邑所侵擊，不得與交州通，故其使罕至。

translations.literal: The people's nature is good; they are not skilled at war, constantly attacked by Linyi, unable to communicate with Jiaozhou—therefore their envoys rarely arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The people are gentle by nature and not skilled in war; they are constantly raided by Linyi and cannot maintain contact with Jiaozhou, so their envoys rarely reach the court.

sentences.zh: 交州斗絕海島，控帶外國，故恃險數不賓。

translations.literal: Jiaozhou stands isolated beyond the sea on islands, controlling and girding foreign states—therefore relying on its perilous position it repeatedly did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou lies cut off across the sea on its islands, commanding the outer kingdoms, and has therefore often withheld submission, trusting in its remote and defensible position.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，刺史張牧卒，交趾人李長仁殺牧北來部曲，據交州叛，數年病死，從弟叔獻嗣事，號令未行，遣使求刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi of Song, Inspector Zhang Mu died; the Jiaozhi man Li Changren killed Mu's northern followers, seized Jiaozhou and rebelled; after several years he died of illness; his younger cousin Shuxian succeeded the affairs, orders not yet enforced, sent envoys requesting an inspector.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Song Taishi era, Inspector Zhang Mu died. Li Changren of Jiaozhi killed Mu's northern troops, seized Jiaozhou, and rebelled. He died of illness after several years, and his younger cousin Shuxian took over before his authority was established and sent envoys requesting an imperial inspector.

sentences.zh: 宋朝以南海太守沈煥為交州刺史，以叔獻為煥寧遠司馬、武平新昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: The Song court appointed Administrator of Nanhai Shen Huan as Inspector of Jiaozhou, and Shuxian as Huan's Ningyuan Major and Administrator of the two commanderies of Wuping and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court appointed Shen Huan, Administrator of Nanhai, as Inspector of Jiaozhou, and made Shuxian Huan's Ningyuan Major and Administrator of Wuping and Xinchang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 叔獻得朝命，人情服從，遂發兵守險不納煥，煥停鬱林病卒。

translations.literal: Shuxian received the court appointment; popular sentiment submitted; then he raised troops to guard the passes and would not admit Huan; Huan halted at Yulin and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shuxian received the court appointment, the people submitted to him; he then raised troops to hold the passes and refused to admit Huan, who halted at Yulin and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖建元元年，仍以叔獻為交州刺史，就安慰之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan of the Founding Emperor, Shuxian was again made Inspector of Jiaozhou, going to comfort and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year 1 of Emperor Gao, Shuxian was again appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou and sent to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 叔獻受命，既而斷割外國，貢獻寡少。

translations.literal: Shuxian received the appointment; afterward he cut off foreign states, and tribute and gifts were few.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxian accepted the appointment, but then cut off the outer kingdoms, and tribute grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 世祖欲討之，永明三年，以司農劉楷為交州刺史，發南康、廬陵、始興郡兵征交州。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wished to attack him; in the third year of Yongming, he appointed Minister of Agriculture Liu Kai as Inspector of Jiaozhou, mobilizing troops from the commanderies of Nankang, Luling, and Shixing to campaign against Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu resolved to punish him. In Yongming year 3 he appointed Liu Kai, Minister of Agriculture, as Inspector of Jiaozhou and mobilized troops from Nankang, Luling, and Shixing to campaign against the province.

sentences.zh: 叔獻聞之，遣使願更申數年，獻十二隊純銀兜鍪及孔雀毦，世祖不許。

translations.literal: Shuxian hearing this sent envoys wishing to extend several more years, offering twelve sets of pure silver helmets and peacock-feather canopies; Emperor Wu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuxian heard of this, he sent envoys asking for several more years' grace and offered twelve sets of pure silver helmets and peacock-feather canopies; Emperor Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 叔獻懼為楷所襲，間道自湘川還朝。

translations.literal: Shuxian feared being struck by Kai; by a hidden route from the Xiang River he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an attack by Liu Kai, Shuxian took a hidden route through the Xiang region and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，以始興太守房法乘代楷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Administrator of Shixing Fang Fachang replaced Kai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Fang Fachang, Administrator of Shixing, replaced Liu Kai.

sentences.zh: 法乘至鎮，屬疾不理事，專好讀書。

translations.literal: Fachang upon reaching his post fell ill and did not handle affairs, devoted solely to reading books.
translations.idiomatic: When Fachang reached his post he fell ill and neglected official business, devoting himself entirely to reading.

sentences.zh: 長史伏登之因此擅權，改易將吏，不令法乘知。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Fu Dengzhi on this account seized power, changing generals and officials without letting Fachang know.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Fu Dengzhi seized power on this account, replacing officers and officials without Fachang's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 錄事房季文白之，法乘大怒，繫登之於獄。

translations.literal: Recorder Fang Jiwen reported this; Fachang was greatly angered and bound Dengzhi in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Fang Jiwen reported this to Fachang, who flew into a rage and had Dengzhi imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，登之厚賂法乘妹夫崔景叔得出，將部曲襲州執法乘，謂之曰：「使君既有疾，不宜勞。」

translations.literal: After ten-odd days, Dengzhi heavily bribed Fachang's brother-in-law Cui Jingshu and got out; leading his personal troops he raided the province, seized Fachang, and said to him: 'My lord, since you have illness, you should not exert yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days, Dengzhi bribed Fachang's brother-in-law Cui Jingshu heavily and got out; he then led his troops in a surprise attack on the provincial seat, seized Fachang, and said to him, 'My lord, since you are ill, you should not overexert yourself.'

sentences.zh: 囚之別室。

translations.literal: He imprisoned him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: He confined him in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 法乘無事，復就登之求書讀，登之曰：「使君靜處猶恐動疾，豈可看書。」

translations.literal: Fachang having nothing to do again went to Dengzhi requesting books to read; Dengzhi said: 'My lord, even resting quietly I still fear your illness may flare—how can you read books?'
translations.idiomatic: With nothing else to do, Fachang asked Dengzhi for books to read. Dengzhi said, 'My lord, even resting quietly I fear your illness may worsen—how can you read books?'

sentences.zh: 遂不與。

translations.literal: Then he did not give them.
translations.idiomatic: And he refused to give him any.

sentences.zh: 乃啟法乘心疾動，不任視事，世祖仍以登之為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Then he reported that Fachang's heart illness had flared, unable to bear overseeing affairs; Emperor Wu still made Dengzhi Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported that Fachang's heart ailment had worsened and that he was unfit to govern; Emperor Wu accordingly appointed Dengzhi Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 法乘還至嶺而卒。

translations.literal: Fachang returned to the mountain passes and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fachang died on the road home before crossing the mountains.

sentences.zh: 法乘，清河人。

translations.literal: Fachang was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fachang was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，為太祖驃騎中兵，至左中郎將。

translations.literal: During Shengming he served the Founding Emperor as Central Army Major of the Piaoqi Commandery, rising to Left Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era he served Emperor Gao as Central Army Major under the Piaoqi Commandery and rose to Left Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 性方簡，身長八尺三寸，行出人上，常自俯屈。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and simple; his body eight chi three inches tall; when walking he rose above others, yet he often bent himself down.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and plain by nature, stood eight chi three inches tall, and though he towered over others when he walked, he usually stooped to avoid seeming overbearing.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史明慶符亦長與法乘等，朝廷唯此二人。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qingzhou Ming Qingfu was also tall and equal to Fachang; in the court only these two men.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Qingfu, Inspector of Qingzhou, was equally tall; in the entire court only these two men matched in height.

translations.literal: Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：書稱「蠻夷猾夏」，蓋總而為言矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Classic says 'the barbarians of Man and Yi trouble Xia'—this is speaking in general terms.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The Classic speaks of 'barbarians troubling the Middle Kingdom'—that is a general statement.

sentences.zh: 至於南夷雜種，分嶼建國，四方珍怪，莫此為先，藏山隱海，瓌寶溢目。

translations.literal: As for the mixed breeds of the southern Yi, dividing islands to establish states, rare wonders of the four directions—none come before this; treasures hidden in mountains and seas, precious gems overflowing the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Among the diverse peoples of the southern Yi, who have founded kingdoms on scattered islands, none surpass them in the rare wonders of the four quarters; treasures lie hidden in mountains and seas, and precious things dazzle the eye.

sentences.zh: 商舶遠屆，委輸南州，故交、廣富實，牣積王府。

translations.literal: Merchant ships arrive from afar; goods are delivered to the southern provinces—therefore Jiao and Guang are rich and full, overflowing and heaped in the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant ships arrive from distant seas and unload their goods in the southern provinces, so Jiaozhou and Guangzhou are rich and prosperous, and the imperial treasury overflows with their tribute.

sentences.zh: 充斥之事差微，聲教之道可被。

translations.literal: Matters of flooding abundance are somewhat reduced; the way of sound teaching can be extended.
translations.idiomatic: Though the burdens of trade and tribute have eased somewhat, the reach of civilizing influence can still be extended.

sentences.zh: 若夫用德以懷遠，其在此乎？

translations.literal: If one uses virtue to embrace the distant—is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: If virtue is to win over distant peoples, is this not the place to begin?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：司、雍分壃，荊及衡陽。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Si and Yong divide the borders; Jing and Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Si and Yong mark the frontier; Jing and Hengyang follow.

sentences.zh: 參錯州部，地有蠻方。

translations.literal: Interwoven and mixed are the provinces and departments; the land has barbarian regions.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and districts interlock here, and barbarian lands lie within.

sentences.zh: 東夷海外，碣石、扶桑。

translations.literal: Eastern Yi beyond the sea—Jieshi, Fusang.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi lie beyond the sea, from Jieshi to Fusang.

sentences.zh: 南域憬遠，極泛溟滄。

translations.literal: The southern realm distant and far, reaching the vast blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: The southern realm stretches far away, reaching the boundless ocean.

sentences.zh: 非要乃貢，竝亦來王。

translations.literal: Not by coercion then tribute; together they also come as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Not by force do they bring tribute—they come willingly to pay homage.
